text: {"brief_summary":"Example Holdings LLC is a group of five companies with about 600 staff in Dubai and Riyadh. Each company has its own shared drives and email newsletters; staff cannot find policies and the group cannot reach everyone with one announcement. The group wants one intranet with news, policies and a staff directory, where each company publishes its own news, group HR publishes to everyone, and staff can search for policies and people. The group uses Microsoft 365, works in Arabic and English, and existing policies sit across five shared drives in different formats. The brief gives no timeline, budget, launch date or success measures.","technology_stack":{"title":"Intranet platform","question":"Which platform should the group intranet be built on?","context":"Fact: the brief says the group uses Microsoft 365 but does not name an intranet product. Fact: it needs news, policies, a staff directory and search, with publishing by each company and by group HR, in Arabic and English. Assumption: staff identities already sit in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) and staff sign in to Microsoft 365 daily. Not stated: whether the five companies share one Microsoft 365 tenant, the budget or the in-house IT skills.","options":[{"key":"sharepoint_viva","title":"SharePoint Online hub with Viva Connections","description":"A SharePoint hub site for the group, with one communication site per company and one for group HR, a policy library, people search from Microsoft 365, and Viva Connections to show the intranet inside Teams.","pros":["Uses Microsoft 365, which the brief says the group already has; little or no extra licence cost assumed","Built-in Arabic and English support, including right-to-left layout and multilingual pages","Hub and site permissions fit 'each company publishes its own news, group HR publishes to everyone'","Microsoft Search covers both policies and people out of the box","Group IT can likely run it without specialist developers"],"cons":["Out-of-the-box design is plain; the brief gives no sign the group has them"]}],"recommended_option":"sharepoint_viva","recommendation_rationale":"The brief's needs (news, policies, directory, search, publishing by company and by group HR, Arabic and English) are standard intranet features that SharePoint and Viva Connections cover, and the group already uses Microsoft 365. This keeps cost and risk low for 600 staff and lets group IT run it. A packaged product is worth considering if the customer wants a more polished look or stronger targeting and accepts licence cost. This is a recommendation for the project team to decide, not a decision.","assumptions":["All five companies are in one Microsoft 365 tenant, or can be brought into one","Most staff have Microsoft 365 licences that include SharePoint","Staff names, roles and companies are recorded in Entra ID","No legal requirement prevents content being stored in the group's existing Microsoft 365 data location"],"risks":["Multiple tenants would complicate the shared directory, search and group-wide news","Poor directory data would make people search unreliable","Arabic content may be under-produced if translation is not resourced","Data residency rules for Saudi Arabia or the UAE may affect where content can be stored"],"source_quotes":["The group uses Microsoft 365.","One intranet for the whole group with news, policies and a staff directory.","Arabic and English are both used."]},"delivery_approach":{"title":"Delivery approach","question":"How should the intranet be delivered and rolled out across the five companies?","context":"Fact: five companies, about 600 staff, in two countries. Not stated: timeline, launch date or whether one company is ready to go first.","options":[{"key":"foundation_then_companies","title":"Group foundation first, then onboard companies one at a time","description":"First release: group hub, group HR news, staff directory, search and the bilingual layout. Then each company is onboarded in turn with its news site and its migrated policies.","pros":["Group HR can reach everyone early, which addresses a stated problem","Policy migration is split into five manageable batches","Lessons from the first company improve the next ones"],"cons":["Some companies wait longer for their own news and policies","Search results are incomplete until all policies are migrated","Needs clear communication about what is and is not available yet"]},{"key":"pilot_then_rollout","title":"Full pilot with one company, then group-wide rollout","description":"Build all features for one company and group HR, test with that company's staff, then roll out to the other four together.","pros":["Tests the whole design with real users before wide release","Fewer launch events"],"cons":["Group-wide announcements wait until the pilot ends","Four companies' policy migrations land at once at rollout"]},{"key":"single_release","title":"Single release for the whole group","description":"Build everything, migrate all policies, and launch to all 600 staff on one date.","pros":["One launch and one training campaign","Staff see a complete intranet from day one"],"cons":["Highest risk: any migration delay holds up the whole launch","No real user feedback before launch","Large migration effort concentrated in one period"]}],"recommended_option":"foundation_then_companies","recommendation_rationale":"The brief names two problems: staff cannot find policies and the group cannot reach everyone. This is a recommendation for the project manager and customer to decide on.","assumptions":["There is no fixed launch date that requires all companies at once","Each company can name a content owner for its news and policies","Group HR is ready to publish soon after the first release"],"risks":["Companies onboarded later may lose interest or keep using shared drives","Policy migration effort per company is unknown until the drives are reviewed","Old email newsletters may run in parallel unless a switch-off is agreed"],"source_quotes":["Existing policies are spread across five shared drives in different formats.","Each company can publish its own news, and group HR can publish to everyone."]},"clarifying_questions":[{"category":"integrations","title":"Microsoft 365 tenant setup","question":"Are all five companies in one Microsoft 365 tenant, or does each company (or country) have its own?","why_it_matters":"A single tenant makes a shared directory, group-wide search and group news straightforward. This is likely the largest work item.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"current_reviewed_only","title":"Only current policies, reviewed by owners","description":"Each company's policy owner confirms which versions are current; only those move, older ones are archived."},{"key":"migrate_all","title":"Move everything as it is","description":"Copy all files from the five drives and tidy up later."},{"key":"rewrite_as_pages","title":"Rewrite key policies as web pages","description":"Main policies become searchable pages in a common format; others stay as documents."}],"recommended_answer":"current_reviewed_only","recommendation_rationale":"The stated problem is that staff cannot find policies; moving old and duplicate versions would carry that problem into the intranet.
